info.title: MoEngage Analytics Query API
info.description:
Asynchronous REST APIs to run MoEngage Analytics queries — Behavior, Funnels, Retention,
Session/Source (BFRS) and User Property Analysis (UPA) — and retrieve their results.

These queries are asynchronous. A `POST` registers the query and immediately returns a
`request_id`; a worker executes the query; you then poll the status and fetch the results:

1. **Submit** — `POST` one of the analysis endpoints. The response echoes the analysis `type` and returns a `request_id`.
2. **Poll** — `GET /v5/analytics/query/{request_id}/status` until `status` is `SUCCESSFUL` (or `FAILED`).
3. **Fetch** — `GET /v5/analytics/query/{request_id}/results` to retrieve the resolved series.

dc.description: The 'dc' in the API Endpoint URL refers to the MoEngage Data Center (DC). MoEngage hosts each customer in a different DC. You can find your DC number and replace the value of 'dc' in the URL by referring to the DC and API endpoint mapping [here](/api/introduction#data-centers). Your MoEngage Data Center (DC) can be 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, or 101.

tags.name: Analytics Queries
tags.description: Register asynchronous BFRS and UPA analytics queries, then poll status and fetch results.

x-mint.content:
#### Rate Limit

The rate limits are at the workspace level. A maximum of 5 requests per second, 20 requests per minute, and 350 requests per hour are allowed per workspace.

post.description:
Registers an asynchronous Behavior analysis query and returns a `request_id`. Behavior analysis measures how many users perform one or more events over a time range, broken down by the dimensions you choose.

Use the `request_id` with [Get Query Status](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-status) to poll for completion, then [Get Query Results](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-results) to fetch the resolved series.

200.description: Query registered. Poll status and fetch results with `data.request_id`.

Use the `request_id` with [Get Query Status](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-status) to poll for completion, then [Get Query Results](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-results) to fetch the resolved series.

post.description:
Registers an asynchronous User Property Analysis (UPA) query and returns a `request_id`. User Property Analysis computes counts, distinct-value counts, distributions, and aggregations over user attributes for a cohort of users.

Use the `request_id` with [Get Query Status](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-status) to poll for completion, then [Get Query Results](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-results) to fetch the resolved series.

200.description: Query registered. Poll status and fetch results with `data.request_id`.

get.description: Returns the execution status of a registered query. Poll this endpoint until the query reaches a terminal status, then fetch the results.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The `request_id` returned when the query was registered.

200.description: This response is returned when the request is processed successfully.

type.description: The type of resource returned in the `data` field.

status.description:
Execution status of the query.

- `PENDING`: The query is registered and queued. Keep polling.
- `PROCESSING`: The query is running. Keep polling.
- `SUCCESSFUL`: The query finished. Fetch the results with [Get Query Results](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-results).
- `FAILED`: The query could not be completed. Check `failure_reason`, correct the request, and register the query again. A `request_id` cannot be re-run.

failure_reason.description: Why the query failed. Returned only when `status` is `FAILED`.
failure_reason.example: One or more selected attributes are no longer available. Please verify your selection and try again.

data.failure_reason: One or more selected attributes are no longer available. Please verify your selection and try again.

get.description:
Returns the resolved results of a completed query, as an array of metric rows.

Every row carries the common fields (`metric`, `granularity`, `splitby`, `tseq`, `cseq`). The remaining fields depend on the analysis type the query was registered for, so handle each row as a flexible set of keys. Select an example below to see the shape returned for each analysis type.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The `request_id` returned when the query was registered.

200.description: This response is returned when the request is processed successfully.

type.description: The type of resource returned in the `data` field.

data.description: The resolved query results, as an array of metric rows.

basicAuth.description:
Authentication is done via Basic Auth. This requires a Base64-encoded string of your credentials in the format `username:password`.

- **Username**: Use your MoEngage Workspace ID (also known as the App ID). Find it in the MoEngage dashboard at **Settings** > **Account** > **API keys**.
- **Password**: Use an API key from **Settings** > **Account** > **API keys**.

Refer to [API Key Dashboard](/user-guide/settings/account/api-and-api-keys/api-key-dashboard) for details on creating and managing API keys.

ResponseId.description: A unique identifier for the response, useful for correlating logs and support requests.

QueryRegistration.description: Acknowledgement that a query was registered. Use `data.request_id` to poll status and fetch results.

type.description: The analysis type echoed back for the registered query.

request_id.description: Identifier of the registered query. Use it with the status and results endpoints.

QueryResultRow.description: A single row of query results. The common fields are present for every analysis type; the remaining fields depend on the analysis the query was registered for.

metric.description: The computed value for this row — a count, rate, or aggregation result.

granularity.description: The time bucket this row belongs to, or `entire` when the result is not time-bucketed.

splitby.description: The key/value breakdown pairs for this row. Empty when the query requested no split.

tseq.description: Time-comparison sequence index. `0` for the primary time range.

cseq.description: Segment-comparison sequence index. `0` for the first segment.

step.description: Behavior and User Analysis: the `id` of the event or user property this row belongs to. Funnels: the funnel step number.

grouped_by.description: Behavior only. The grouping values applied to this row.

split_by_weight.description: Funnels only. The base denominator used to calculate the conversion rate for this step.

total_users.description: Retention only. The size of the cohort for this period.

retained_user.description: Retention only. The number of users from the cohort who returned.

retention_comparison_index.description: Retention only. The offset, in periods, from the cohort period.

retention_compared_by.description: Retention only. The label of the period being compared against.

analysis_type.description: Session/Source only. Echoes the `report_type` the query requested.

event_name.description: Session/Source only. The underlying system event the metric is derived from.

bucket.description: User Analysis only. The property value or distribution bucket this row represents, formatted according to the property's requested projection.

AttributeReference.description: A reference to an event, user, or device attribute used for grouping, splitting, or aggregating results.

attr_type.description: The category the attribute belongs to, such as `event`, `user`, `device`, or `source`.

column_name.description: The stored name of the attribute.

readable_name.description: The attribute's display name, as shown in the MoEngage dashboard.

type.description: The internal type code for the attribute's data type, such as `_s` for string or `_f` for a numeric value.

data_types.description: The data types accepted for this attribute.

encrypted.description: Whether the attribute is stored encrypted.

pii.description: Whether the attribute is marked as personally identifiable information.

SourceAttributeReference.description: A reference to an acquisition attribute, such as source, medium, or campaign, used to group Session/Source results.

attr_type.description: The category the attribute belongs to.

column_name.description: The stored name of the acquisition attribute.

readable_name.description: The attribute's display name, as shown in the MoEngage dashboard.

type.description: The internal type code for the attribute's data type.

data_types.description: The data types accepted for this attribute.

UserAttributeReference.description: A reference to a user attribute used for splitting User Analysis results.

attr_type.description: The category the attribute belongs to.

name.description: The stored name of the user attribute.

readable_name.description: The attribute's display name, as shown in the MoEngage dashboard.

encrypted.description: Whether the attribute is stored encrypted.

pii.description: Whether the attribute is marked as personally identifiable information.

BucketDistribution.description: Bucketing configuration for a distribution analysis. Use `auto` to let MoEngage choose the buckets, or `custom` to define your own range and interval.

type.description: Whether buckets are chosen automatically or defined by you.

from.description: The lower bound of the first bucket. Use -1 when `type` is `auto`.

to.description: The upper bound of the last bucket. Use -1 when `type` is `auto`.

interval.description: The width of each bucket. Use -1 when `type` is `auto`.

FunnelAttributeMeta.description: Describes which funnel steps an attribute is applied to.

type.description: The steps the attribute applies to, such as `all_steps`, the first N steps, or a specific step.

applied_on.description: The step number the attribute applies to. Use -1 when the attribute applies to all steps.

FunnelDistribution.description: Distribution configuration for a time-to-convert or frequency funnel, defining the step range measured and how results are bucketed.

method.description: Whether buckets are chosen automatically or defined by you.

from_step.description: The step the measurement starts from.

to_step.description: The step the measurement ends at.

parameters.description: The range measured and the size of each bucket.

range.description: The overall range the distribution covers.

multiplier.description: The unit the range is measured in, such as `MINUTE`, `HOUR`, or `DAY`.

bucket.description: The size of each individual bucket.

size.description: The number of units in each bucket.

multiplier.description: The unit the bucket size is measured in.

EventAggregation.description: The aggregation applied to a numeric event attribute, such as a sum or a percentile.

operation.description: The aggregation to compute, such as `sum`, `min`, `max`, `average`, `median`, or a percentile.

attr.description: The attribute the aggregation is computed over.

percentile_value.description: The percentile to compute, from 1 to 100, when `operation` is a percentile. Use -1 for all other operations.

FilterGroup.description: A group of filter criteria combined by a logical operator. Used to define segmentation and event-level conditions.

included_filters.description: Criteria a user must match. For the supported filter payload and fields, see [Create Filter Segment](/api/filter-segments/create-filter-segment).

filter_operator.description: The logical operator used to combine the filters in this group.

filters.description: The individual filter criteria. Each item is a filter object whose structure varies by `filter_type` (common values: `actions`, `user_attributes`, `custom_segments`).

Segmentation.description: Segments used to scope the analysis to a subset of users. Include up to 5 segments. To analyze all users, pass a single segment with the `All Users` custom segment.

Timerange.description: The time window the analysis runs over.

start.description: Start of the window, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (workspace time zone).

end.description: End of the window, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (workspace time zone).

label.description: Human-readable label for the window, as shown in the dashboard.

dt_label.description: Relative-range keyword the label maps to.

value.description: Numeric component of a relative range (for example, 7 for the last 7 days).

BehaviorQueryRequest.description: Request body for registering a Behavior analysis query.

type.description: The analysis type. Must be `behavior` for this endpoint.

analysis_type.description: The behavior metric to compute — for example, `events` (event counts), `users` (users who performed the event), or a per-user aggregation.

events.description: The events to analyze. Include 1 to 10 events. Each event has an `id`, one or more `actions` (event + attribute filters), an optional `split_by`, and an optional `aggregation`.

id.description: Identifier for the event within this query (for example, `A`).

actions.description: The event and attribute conditions that define this event.

split_by.description: Attributes to break this event down by. The combined total of all `split_by` entries and `user_attr_grouped_by` must not exceed 10.

aggregation.description: The aggregation applied to this event, used when `analysis_type` is an aggregation. Pass an empty object for other analysis types.

user_attr_grouped_by.description: User attributes to group the results by. Include up to 10; the combined total with all `split_by` entries must not exceed 10.

distribution.description: Custom distribution configuration. When using custom buckets, include at most 10 buckets. Pass an empty object for no custom distribution.

granularity.description: Time bucket for the series — `h` (hour), `d` (day), `w` (week), `m` (month), or `e` (entire range). When hourly, the time range must not exceed 31 days.

count_type.description: Whether metrics are returned as absolute counts (`number`) or as percentages (`percentage`).

chart_plot_type.description: Plot scale applied to the chart.

rolling_value.description: Rolling-window size for the metric, or -1 when not used.

user_aggregation_type.description: The per-user aggregation to apply. Empty when not using an aggregation.

user_aggregation_percentile.description: Percentile to compute when `user_aggregation_type` is a percentile aggregation. A value from 1 to 100, or -1 when not used.

comparison_timerange.description: A second time range to compare against. Time comparison is supported only on line, bar, and column charts, and cannot be combined with custom-segment comparison (2 or more segments). Pass an empty object for no comparison.

chart_sort_type.description: Sort order applied to the result series.

FunnelsQueryRequest.description: Request body for registering a Funnels analysis query.

type.description: The analysis type. Must be `funnel` for this endpoint.

events.description: The ordered steps of the funnel. Include 2 to 10 steps. Each step defines the event and attribute conditions a user must satisfy to be counted at that step.

step_number.description: The 1-based position of this step in the funnel.

step_type.description: Whether users who match this step are included in or excluded from the funnel.

from_step.description: For a distribution funnel, the step the window is measured from. Null otherwise.

to_step.description: For a distribution funnel, the step the window is measured to. Null otherwise.

funnel_type.description: The kind of funnel to compute. The `user_` values count unique users and the `event_` values count all occurrences — `user_funnel` and `event_funnel` (standard conversion), `user_time_to_convert` and `event_time_to_convert` (time-to-convert distribution between two steps), and `user_frequency` and `event_frequency` (frequency distribution of repeated actions between two steps).

grouped_by.description: Event attributes to split the funnel by. Include up to 3. Each item names the attribute to split on.

grouped_by_meta.description: Describes how each `grouped_by` attribute is applied across the funnel — for example, to all steps, to the first N steps, or to a specific step. Keys correspond to the attributes in `grouped_by`. Pass an empty object when `grouped_by` is empty.

holding_attributes.description: Event attributes that must hold the same value across funnel steps, so only users who kept that value are counted as converted. Include up to 3.

holding_attributes_meta.description: Describes how each holding attribute is applied across the funnel steps. Keys correspond to the attributes in `holding_attributes`. Pass an empty object when `holding_attributes` is empty.

funnel_window.description: The conversion window in seconds within which users must complete the funnel.

funnel_window_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the funnel window.

strict_order.description: Whether steps must be performed in the exact order defined.

distribution.description: Distribution configuration for `event_time_to_convert` and `user_frequency` funnels. When using custom buckets, include at most 25 buckets. Pass an empty object for a standard funnel.

countType.description: Whether metrics are returned as absolute counts (`number`) or as percentages (`percentage`).

showConversionEventOnly.description: Whether to return only the conversion event's metrics.

comparison_timerange.description: A second time range to compare against. Time comparison is supported only on line, bar, and column charts, and cannot be combined with custom-segment comparison (2 or more segments). Pass an empty object for no comparison.

granularity.description: Time bucket for the series — `h` (hour), `d` (day), `w` (week), `m` (month), or `e` (entire range). When hourly, the time range must not exceed 31 days.

chart_plot_type.description: Plot scale applied to the chart.

RetentionQueryRequest.description: Request body for registering a Retention analysis query.

type.description: The analysis type. Must be `retention` for this endpoint.

events.description: Exactly two events: the `first` event that places a user into a cohort, and the `return` event measured in later periods.

id.description: The event's role in the analysis.

actions.description: The event and attribute conditions that define this event.

segmentation.description: Segments to scope the analysis (up to 5). Segmentation and `comparison_timerange` are mutually exclusive — do not send 2 or more segments together with a time comparison.

granularity.description: Cohort period — `h` (hour), `d` (day), `w` (week), `m` (month), or `e` (entire range). Hourly is limited to a 24-hour window, daily to 90 days, and weekly to 180 days.

retention_type.description: The retention model to apply — `every` for N-Day retention (users who returned in that specific period), `last` for Unbounded retention (users who returned in that period or any later one), or `first` for First Occurrence retention (users whose first return fell in that period).

split_by.description: Attributes to break the cohorts down by. Include up to 10.

comparison_timerange.description: A second time range to compare against. Mutually exclusive with sending 2 or more segments. Pass an empty object for no comparison.

SessionSourceQueryRequest.description: Request body for registering a Session/Source analysis query.

type.description: The analysis type. Must be `session-source` for this endpoint.

report_type.description: The session metric to compute — session count, average session duration, average sessions per user, average conversions per session, conversion count, revenue, or bounce rate.

filters.description: Conditions that restrict the report to specific acquisition values. Combined with `grouped_by`, at most 2 source properties may be used. A filter value must match the attribute's declared data type.

attr_type.description: The category the attribute belongs to.

column_name.description: The acquisition property to filter on, such as source, medium, or campaign.

type.description: The internal type code for the attribute's data type.

data_types.description: The data types accepted for this attribute.

encrypted.description: Whether the attribute is stored encrypted.

condition.description: The condition applied to the attribute.

grouped_by.description: Acquisition properties to break the report down by (for example, source and medium). Include up to 2.

granularity.description: Time bucket for the series — `h` (hour), `d` (day), `w` (week), `m` (month), or `e` (entire range). When hourly, the time range must not exceed 31 days.

count_type.description: Whether metrics are returned as absolute counts (`number`) or as percentages (`percentage`).

comparison_timerange.description: A second time range to compare against. Time comparison is supported only on line, bar, and column charts, and cannot be combined with custom-segment comparison (2 or more segments). Pass an empty object for no comparison.

chart_sort_type.description: Sort order applied to the result series.

UserAnalysisQueryRequest.description: Request body for registering a User Property Analysis (UPA) query.

type.description: The analysis type. Must be `user_analysis` for this endpoint.

analysis_type.description: The user-property computation to run — `total_count` (all users in scope), `distinct_count` (distinct values of the attribute), `distribution` (how users are spread across the attribute's values, using automatic or custom buckets), `aggregation` (sum, minimum, maximum, average, median, or percentile), or `email_domain_analysis`.

user_properties.description: The user attributes to analyze. Include 1 to 5 properties. When more than one is provided, results are cross-tabulated across them.

id.description: Identifier for this property within the query (for example, `A`).

property.description: The attribute definition and any attribute-level filters.

filter_type.description: The kind of attribute being analyzed.

executed.description: Whether the attribute condition must be satisfied.

execution.description: Execution criteria for the attribute condition.

pii.description: Whether the attribute is marked as personally identifiable information.

encrypted.description: Whether the attribute is stored encrypted.

projection.description: How the attribute's value is formatted before results are grouped. For example, a datetime attribute projected as a date returns buckets like `19 May 2023`, and a boolean attribute returns the strings `true` and `false`. Pass an empty object to use the attribute's raw value.

extract_type.description: The part of the value to project — for example, `date` to bucket a datetime attribute by calendar date.

object_projection.description: Projection configuration for object-type attributes, naming the nested key within the object to analyze. Pass an empty object for non-object attributes.

aggregation.description: The aggregation to compute when `analysis_type` is `aggregation` — for example sum, minimum, maximum, average, median, distinct count, or a percentile from 1 to 100. Pass an empty object for other analysis types.

distribution.description: Distribution configuration. Custom distributions apply to numerical attributes only. Use `type: auto` for automatic bucketing.

granularity.description: Time bucket for the series — `d` (day), `w` (week), `m` (month), `y` (year), or `e` (entire range).

count_type.description: Whether metrics are returned as absolute counts (`number`) or as percentages (`percentage`).

split_by.description: Attributes to break the result down by. Include up to 10.

chart_sort_type.description: Sort order applied to the result series.

GatewayAuthError.description: Authentication or authorization failure returned by the API gateway. The body is JSON, but the gateway sends it with `Content-Type: text/plain`.

code.description: A machine-readable code identifying the failure, such as `ER001` when credentials are missing or invalid, or `ER007` when the credentials do not have access to the route.

target.description: The stage of the request that failed.

message.description: A human-readable description of the failure.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard MoEngage error envelope, returned by the service. Authentication and authorization failures (401 and 403) are returned by the API gateway in a different format — see those responses for details.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.

doc_url.description: A link to documentation about this error, when available.

ValidationFailed.description: Validation failed — a required field is missing, a value is invalid, or a documented limit is exceeded.

error.message: analysis_type - Enum doesnt allow value: eventsdfg, allowed values: [events, users, session, aggregation, aggregation_distribution, total_events_per_user, attribute_aggregation_per_user] : 'eventsdfg'

Unauthorized.description:
This response is returned when the credentials are missing or invalid.

The API gateway generates this response before the request reaches the service, so it does not use the standard error envelope. The body is JSON, but the gateway sends it with `Content-Type: text/plain`. Parse it accordingly.

Forbidden.description:
This response is returned when the credentials are valid but do not have access to this route or workspace.

The API gateway generates this response before the request reaches the service, so it does not use the standard error envelope. The body is JSON, but the gateway sends it with `Content-Type: text/plain`. Parse it accordingly.

QueryFailed.description: This response is returned when the query did not complete successfully, so no results are available. Check the `failure_reason` on [Get Query Status](/api/analytics-queries/get-query-status), correct the request, and register the query again.

error.message: Query failed as column not found

NotFound.description: The query `request_id` does not exist, or is not in this workspace.

error.message: The query request you are looking for does not exist.

QuotaExceeded.description: This response is returned when the workspace has reached its monthly Fair Usage Policy (FUP) limit for analytics usage.

error.message: Your workspace has reached its monthly Fair Usage Policy limit for analytics usage. Please contact your Customer Success Manager to expand your quota.
An unexpected error occurred while processing the request.
